more_info.overview: Cellulose is used as an emulsifier in food. Its technological role is to help oil and water remain mixed.
more_info.uses: EU permissions include unflavoured live fermented cream products and substitute products, both with a fat  content of less than 20 %, table-top sweeteners in powder form, table-top sweeteners in tablets, herbs and spices. These permissions depend on the food category and its conditions of use.
more_info.origin: Cellulose pulp comes from fibrous plant material. Microcrystalline cellulose is purified and partly broken down with mineral acid, while powdered cellulose is purified and mechanically reduced.
more_info.dietary_restrictions: The specified starting material is plant derived and compatible with vegetarian and vegan diets. The specification does not establish halal or kosher certification.
more_info.side_effects:
Assessed food uses raised no concern.
High-dose animal studies found no reproductive or developmental harm.
